description: P4-B of PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_PLAN.md: the GENERATION LOOP -- propose -> build -> verify -> accept/counterexample/gap -- as seed rules; the LLM-analog core loop (plan par.2). Every status transition is a rule; the adapter (domains/prog_synthesis.py) only records facts, splices rule-decided templates into hub IR, evaluates bound Terms (ProgEval over the REFLECTED IR subgraph) and applies results -- the _enact_advance precedent. THE OCCAM LADDER, enforced by guards: rung 1 codebook propose (ps_propose: Argmax by trigger specificity over eligible code_write_construction quanta; ShapeDecode residual recorded as decode evidence) -> rung 1.5 sequencing (ps_route_lattice when the winning template is STATEMENT-grain: Hyp/LatEdge lattice scored by P3 ConstructionBigram trans_logp, decoded by the UNCHANGED seeds/viterbi_decode.json vit_step/vit_backtrace on a throwaway substrate -- the ink_decode._lattice_partition precedent) -> verify (ProgEval per ExampleRow; the RULE decides pass/fail per row and overall; reflect round-trip is the structural verdict) -> accept (ONE Program{name, program} node + reflected subgraph) OR counterexample (CEGIS-as-rules: failing row -> CounterExample node; Excluded node retires the failed plan; bounded integer attempt budget) -> rung 3 enumerate (ps_enumerate_mark ONLY when the codebook is exhausted and examples exist; the SynthEnumerate Term is the P4-A seam -- the adapter feature-detects it and records ps_enumerate_outcome; rules read only the outcome fact, so wiring the landed Term is zero rule changes) -> gap (ps_gap_file: SelfConcern{kind:'code_write'}, the seeds/code_write_gap.json node shape verbatim, content-deduped). CODEBOOK RECONCILIATION (documented in PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_P4B.md): the WRITE codebook (code_write_construction, term/stmts templates) PROPOSES CONTENT; the P3 prog_construction codebook is variant-grain RECOGNITION shapes -- its statement-HEAD labels + the P3 bigram statistics (boarded onto the agent as ConstructionBigram nodes at head grain by the adapter, consuming P3 residual 4) SCORE THE SEQUENCE. This seed also ships ONE statement-grain write shape (sum_of_list_spine, spine=1, trigger TALLY) whose template parts are DELIBERATELY SHUFFLED -- the spine order is the lattice's corpus-statistics decision, proven by the gate. v1.1.0 (P6.5): ps_enumerate_fresh_attempt closes the powered battery's stalled:evaluated defect (PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_P6_BATTERY.md par.2.1) -- when the enumerate rung follows a consumed codebook attempt, the rung's evaluation now gets a FRESH attempt number, so the per-row verdict guard re-arms and the goal always reaches a terminal status (accepted or gapped), never a non-terminal park. v1.2.0 (P7-A, PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_P7_PREREG.md H7a): RECURSIVE DESCENT -- 'shapedecode will tell you what is going on': when the codebook rung is spent but the decode shows PARTIAL cover on a list-input spec (the whole-goal enumerator's inadmissibility boundary), the goal DESCENDS instead of enumerating: covered spans instantiate their construction templates as a skeleton, each uncovered span becomes a Hole whose position comes from the decode assignment (fold accumulator-step inside a covered Fold template; final expression over live vars v_i = covered constructions evaluated per row), the adapter MECHANICALLY derives the hole's local (input, expected) rows where the skeleton makes them determinable (one-iteration unroll for singleton-list rows; prefix evaluation for live vars -- a RULE judges derivability from the recorded facts), the hole becomes a sub-Goal that runs the SAME ladder (hole-scoped enumeration: small holes, big reach), and the accepted sub-IR is spliced back with the FULL outer rows as the fold-up verdict (execution verdict at every level; descent-scoped fu_* row facts, never the eval_attempt lane -- the P6.5 collision cannot re-arm). Depth is integer-bounded (ps_max_depth=2); descent-exhausted goals still reach whole-goal enumerate then gap; codebook-covered and scalar-row requests never descend (guard-proven). v1.3.0 (P7-B, PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_P7_PREREG.md H7b): TRACE-GUIDED LOCAL REPAIR -- an externally-observed failing row on an ACCEPTED goal (ingest_counterexample, mechanical) refutes the accept (ps_repair_mark); the adapter records boundary facts (record_trace: prefix evaluations vs expectations DERIVED by descent's own row-derivation machinery) and the rules localize the fault to the folded hole (ps_localize_hole) or honestly refuse (ps_localize_refuse_* -> the untouched global CEGIS path). Repair re-opens ONLY the localized hole: the counterexample propagates INTO the hole's derived row set (this is what kills first-fit overfitting -- P7-A residual 1), the refuted candidate is an ExcludedSub at hole scope, and the UNCHANGED descent machinery re-solves/splices/re-verifies the FULL rows. Integer repair budget on its own counter lane (ps_repair_attempts/ps_repair_budget); exhaustion -> global path -> gap (ps_repair_exhausted). The skeleton is never re-proposed. v1.4.0 (Arc2 Q4, PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC2_PLAN.md/PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC2_Q4_NOTES.md): DESCENT + REPAIR WIDENING, closing arc-1's registered scope cuts now that MBPP gives them mass. (1) SCALAR-LOOP DESCENT: ps_descend_mark's scope guard widens from list-input-only to ALSO admit a scalar spec whose sole cover is a range()-sourced Fold (tmpl_scalar_fold) -- two new codebook constructions (factorial_of_n_spine / range_sum_spine) give it real triggers; fold_step's row derivation generalizes from 'a singleton LIST row' to 'the Fold source materializes to exactly one element' (domains/prog_synthesis.py's _fold_source_singleton), unifying the list and scalar cases in one formula. (2) BRANCH-ARM HOLES: a NEW plan (ps_plan_branch_arm) fires when the sole cover is an IfThenElse template (tmpl_branch) -- the decided CONDITION is kept from the covered template (P7-A's 'skeleton keeps its structure, only the part in question changes' precedent) and BOTH arms are solved directly (one SynthEnumerate call per row-partition, no further sub-goal recursion -- a scope-limited but real closure of the P7-A named blocker) then recombined into one IfThenElse at fold-up. (3) EXCLUDE-POWERED ITERATION: run_enumerate now threads BOTH the hole-scope ExcludedSub terms (repair's existing per-hole exclusion, now actually reaching the engine's `exclude` param instead of only the coarse const-drop heuristic) AND a NEW top-level round-bounded lane (ps_enum_round/ps_enum_round_budget, ExcludedTerm nodes, the ps_enum_retry_mark rule) that retries a repair-refuted FLAT rung-3 accept with the wrong candidate excluded via the engine contract -- closing the P7-B 'within-round candidate iteration ... contract-blocked for output-valued Lits' residual at the level P7-B could not reach (no Rust in that phase). (4) ROW-VERDICT WIDENING: two new rules (ps_row_pass_special/ps_row_fail_special) consume Q2's mbpp_spec row schema (tol -> float-within-tolerance; unordered -> set/duplicate-insensitive equality) via a recorded comparison fact (cmp_ok, a fixed formula computed by eval_and_record) -- the decision stays a rule; the comparison a fixed formula. Every edit to an EXISTING rule (ps_goal, ps_descend_mark, ps_plan_final_expr, ps_exclude_failed, ps_ce_exhausted, ps_row_pass, ps_row_fail) adds ONLY a clause that is trivially satisfied for every pre-Q4 scenario (a brand-new attr/state that could not previously exist), so every arc-1/P7-A/P7-B gate stays byte-identical. v1.9.0 adds the Arc5 EXACT-FIRST rung (ps_exact_mark/ps_exact_solved/ps_exact_failed): shape -> IR via seeds/exact_families.json's held ExactFamily data, Occam-ordered between descent and enumerate.

microtheory.name: program_synthesis
microtheory.description: an NL spec becomes a Goal; held write-constructions propose, corpus bigrams sequence, execution decides (ProgEval on example rows), a counterexample retires a failed plan, exhaustion files a gap -- the whole generation loop as one run_rules fixpoint with mechanical adapter I/O at the rim.

attrs.name: sum_of_list_spine
attrs.ground_template: {"desc": "returns the running tally of a list of numbers", "mode": "code_write_stmts", "args": ["items"], "stmts": [{"type": "ProgReturn", "value": {"type": "Var", "name": "acc"}}, {"type": "ProgForEach", "var": "x", "iter": {"type": "Var", "name": "items"}, "body": {"type": "ProgAugAssign", "name": "acc", "op": "add", "value": {"type": "Var", "name": "x"}}, "orelse": null}, {"type": "ProgAssignVar", "name": "acc", "value": {"type": "Lit", "value": 0}}]}

rules.name: ps_goal
rules.comment: GOAL MINT: a Message the EXISTING write-request cue machinery marked (code_writing.looks_like_write_request over the held code_write_request_cues Concepts -- the adapter records the verdict as ps_write_request, the _write_function_reply outcome-datum precedent) becomes Goal{kind:synth_program, status:pending}. Mint-once per Message via ps_goal_minted. Budget is an in-frame INTEGER (3 attempts). v1.2.0 (P7-A): the Goal carries ps_depth (copied from the Message; 0 for a top-level request, hole-depth for a descent sub-spec) and the integer descent budget ps_max_depth (2). v1.3.0 (P7-B): the Goal also carries the REPAIR counter lane -- ps_repair_attempts/ps_repair_budget (integer, 2) and ps_repair_seq/ps_trace_seq (the trace freshness pair, -1 sentinel) -- its own integers, separate from ps_attempts by construction (the P6.5 collision discipline at repair grain). v1.4.0 (Arc2-Q4): the Goal also carries the ENUMERATE-RETRY counter lane -- ps_enum_round/ps_enum_round_budget (integer, 2) -- its own lane, separate from ps_attempts/ps_budget and ps_repair_attempts/ps_repair_budget by construction. v1.5.0 (Arc3-R1): scoped to DESCENT SUB-GOALS only (ps_depth != 0) -- a top-level request (ps_depth==0) now mints via the NEW ps_goal_top rule instead, which enters the retrieval ladder before the codebook rung. Byte-identical for every sub-goal mint (depth>=1 was always the sub-goal case).

rules.name: ps_propose
rules.comment: RUNG 1 -- PROPOSE from the WRITE codebook: the winner is the Argmax over eligible (trigger-matching, non-excluded) code_write_construction quanta by SPECIFICITY (trigger-token count -- most specific matching construction first; the code_reading._winner kind-filtered argmax, migrated into the rule). ps_plan_residual records the ShapeDecode of the request skeleton against the held codebook (decode evidence / gap provenance). Attempt counter increments HERE -- one propose == one attempt. v1.5.1 (Arc3-R2.5): a candidate only counts as ELIGIBLE for this propose pick if EITHER the goal is NOT SCREENABLE (DESCEND_APPLICABLE -- the SAME 3-part predicate ps_descend_mark/ps_enumerate_mark embed -- OR no example rows exist -- ps_built_unverifiable stays reachable -- OR slack already exists in the INITIAL trigger-matching pool vs the budget, `ps_screen_pool0` -- every one of these cases is BYTE-IDENTICAL to pre-R2.5 propose), OR this SPECIFIC candidate has already been screened-and-passed (ps_screen_passed, minted by ps_screen_admit). A goal that IS screenable therefore proposes NOTHING until ps_screen_mark/ps_screen_admit has verified the winner off-attempt -- the codebook-side half of the universal execution screen, scoped this time (SCREENABLE) to avoid BOTH Attempt 1's false-negative on partial-cover constructions (PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC3_R12_NOTES.md) AND a second, measured false-positive against `test_prog_synthesis_battery_migrated.py`'s frozen `br_19_pick_or_boost` row (a codebook-decoy-then-enumerate accept that already had enough attempt-budget slack to succeed unscreened).

rules.name: ps_route_lattice
rules.comment: RUNG 1.5 ROUTE: the chosen construction is STATEMENT-grain (spine==1 on the quantum) -- the plan needs a multi-statement spine, so the goal routes through the Hyp/LatEdge lattice (vit_step/vit_backtrace over ConstructionBigram trans_logp -- P3's corpus statistics deciding the order).

rules.name: ps_route_bind
rules.comment: Expression-grain template (no spine attr): straight to slot-binding; no lattice.

rules.name: ps_latticed
rules.comment: The adapter stamped the lattice mechanically and the decoded on_path sequence is a permutation of the template parts (ps_spine_ok -- a recorded FACT, ink's fixed-formula class). The spine order is DECIDED; on to binding.

rules.name: ps_lattice_failed
rules.comment: The decoded sequence was NOT a valid permutation of the parts (the ordering lattice permits label repeats -- an honest recorded residual): the plan is treated as a failed proposal -- exclude it and re-arm. v1.5.0 (Arc3-R1): hand-off is `pending` (STALE PROSE FIXED, Arc3-R2.5 -- an earlier draft of this comment claimed a `pending -> screen_pending` detour that no shipped effect ever performed; the Attempt-1 codebook screen was reverted before this rule's own hand-off ever changed). v1.5.1 (Arc3-R2.5): re-arming to `pending` now DOES re-enter the universal screen when the goal is SCREENABLE (ps_screen_mark), via ps_propose's own widened eligibility gate -- no change to THIS rule's effects, only to what `pending` means downstream.

rules.name: ps_built
rules.comment: The adapter spliced the winning template into concrete hub IR (ps_ir, mechanical) for THIS attempt, and the spec has example rows -- the verdict rung is execution, so on to evaluation.

rules.name: ps_built_unverifiable
rules.comment: IR built but the spec carries NO example rows: the P4 verdict is EXECUTION AGREEMENT with the spec examples (scope pin), so an example-free build cannot be verified -- honest gap-eligible status, never an unverified accept.

rules.name: ps_evaluated
rules.comment: The adapter ran ProgEval over the REFLECTED IR subgraph per example row and recorded got/eval_ok facts (mechanical), plus the reflect round-trip fact ps_reflect_ok. The rows are ready for the verdict rules.

rules.name: ps_row_pass
rules.comment: PER-ROW VERDICT (pass): the evaluation completed (halted, no trap => eval_ok) and the result Eq-agrees with the expected value. The DECISION is this rule's; the adapter only recorded the facts. v1.4.0 (Arc2-Q4): scoped to plain rows (Not the tol/unordered flags) -- ps_row_pass_special/ps_row_fail_special own those; byte-identical pre-Q4 (neither flag attr existed).

rules.name: ps_row_fail
rules.comment: PER-ROW VERDICT (fail): trap/non-halt OR result disagrees. v1.4.0 (Arc2-Q4): same scoping as ps_row_pass, for the same reason.

rules.name: ps_verified
rules.comment: OVERALL VERDICT: every example row of the CURRENT attempt passed (none missing, none failed), and the structural verdict holds (reflect round-trip byte-stable, ps_reflect_ok). ALL rows agree => verified.

rules.name: ps_counterexample
rules.comment: CEGIS AS A RULE: a failing row of the current attempt becomes a CounterExample NODE bound to the Goal (once per row per attempt via ce_attempt). The goal leaves the verified path for re-proposal.

rules.name: ps_exclude_failed
rules.comment: RE-PROPOSE GUARD: the failed construction is retired for this goal via an Excluded node (edge to a NEW node -- the engine cannot add_edge to a Term-found node, the sd_dedup_existing limitation, so exclusion is its own node). Mint-once per name via the Not-Exists guard. v1.4.0 (Arc2-Q4): mutually exclusive with the new ps_enum_retry_mark lever (its negated eligibility predicate) -- a repair-refuted FLAT rung-3 accept with rounds left retries enumerate-with-exclude instead of the codebook-name exclusion path; byte-identical pre-Q4 (the predicate is newly-possible-only).

rules.name: ps_reproposal
rules.comment: Exclusion applied and attempts remain (integer budget): re-arm to pending -- ps_propose re-decides against the codebook MINUS the excluded plan(s). v1.5.0 (Arc3-R1): hand-off is `pending` (STALE PROSE FIXED, Arc3-R2.5 -- see ps_lattice_failed's own comment for the correction). v1.5.1 (Arc3-R2.5): re-arming to `pending` now DOES re-enter the universal screen when the goal is SCREENABLE (ps_screen_mark), via ps_propose's own widened eligibility gate -- no change to THIS rule's effects, only to what `pending` means downstream.

rules.name: ps_ce_exhausted
rules.comment: BUDGET HONESTY: exclusion applied but the attempt budget is spent -- honest exhaustion, never attempt N+1. v1.4.0 (Arc2-Q4): same mutual-exclusion guard as ps_exclude_failed, for the same reason.

rules.name: ps_exhausted
rules.comment: BUDGET HONESTY at the propose gate: pending with the budget spent (candidates may even remain) -- exhausted.

rules.name: ps_enumerate_mark
rules.comment: RUNG 3 -- ENUMERATE (Occam-ordered LAST before gap): only when NO eligible codebook construction remains AND example rows exist (SynthEnumerate is spec-driven; an example-free request has nothing to enumerate against) AND attempts remain. The adapter evaluates the SynthEnumerate Term IF the engine provides it (P4-A seam) and records the outcome fact; the rules only ever read ps_enumerate_outcome -- wiring the landed Term is ZERO rule changes. v1.2.0 (P7-A): now rung 3 BELOW descent -- when descent is applicable (partial cover + a list-input row + depth budget) the enumerator waits for ps_descend_done; everywhere descent cannot apply the guard is identically true and the rung is byte-unchanged. v1.4.0 (Arc2-Q4): the embedded descend-applicability check (the P7-A DESCEND_APPLICABLE constant baked into this rule's own where) widens IDENTICALLY to ps_descend_mark's own guard -- otherwise rung 3 would race ahead of the newly-admitted scalar/branch descent cases (a real bug, caught empirically: without this companion edit rung 3 fires before ps_descend_mark ever gets a chance). Byte-unchanged pre-Q4 for the same reason as (b). v1.10.0 (PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC5_MOVES.md): a NEW mutual-exclusion arm -- ps_rung_moves==1 (the MOVE A/B rung ran, whatever the outcome) OR the goal was never moves-eligible at all (ps_moves_eligible!=1, so ps_move_mark's own guard could never have fired) -- makes the RUNG 2.6 -> RUNG 3 ordering STRUCTURAL rather than a reliance on engine tie-break order between two independently-guarded rules (the SAME discipline ps_move_mark itself uses against ps_exact_mark). Byte-identical for every goal that was never moves-eligible in the first place (the second Or-arm is true immediately, exactly as before this edit).

rules.name: ps_enumerate_fresh_attempt
rules.comment: P6.5 STALL FIX (the powered battery's stalled:evaluated defect, PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_P6_BATTERY.md par.2.1): when the enumerate rung follows a CONSUMED codebook attempt, the example rows already carry eval_attempt == ps_attempts, so ps_row_pass/ps_row_fail's verdict_attempt < eval_attempt guard could never re-arm and the goal parked on the non-terminal 'evaluated' status. THIS RULE gives the enumerate rung's evaluation a FRESH attempt number: on enumerate_pending, iff some example row's eval_attempt equals the goal's CURRENT ps_attempts (the exact collision that defines the defect -- nothing else), ps_attempts += 1 (in-frame integer step). Self-extinguishing: the bump falsifies its own Exists guard, and ps_enumerate_mark is once-guarded (ps_rung_enumerate), so at most one bump per goal. Budget honesty intact: the mark required attempts < budget, so attempts <= budget after the bump, and the downstream exhaustion rules (ps_reproposal / ps_ce_exhausted) keep the integer bound. Every non-colliding path -- fresh enumerate at attempts 0, pure codebook goals -- is byte-unchanged.

rules.name: ps_no_shape
rules.comment: No eligible construction and either no examples to enumerate against OR the enumerate rung already ran (marked): nothing on any rung can build this -- gap-eligible. The Or-arm closes the enumerated-candidate-failed re-entry (a rare DSL-vs-ProgEval divergence case).

rules.name: ps_enumerated
rules.comment: SynthEnumerate produced a fitting term (adapter recorded outcome=ok + spliced ps_ir): the enumerated candidate goes through the SAME execution verdict as every other build.

rules.name: ps_enumerate_unavailable
rules.comment: The engine does not (yet) provide SynthEnumerate (P4-A in flight): the rung files its honest status and falls through to the gap rule. NOT an error -- a recorded capability boundary.

rules.name: ps_enumerate_failed
rules.comment: SynthEnumerate ran but found no fitting program (or trapped): honest failure status, then gap.

rules.name: ps_gap_status
rules.comment: Terminal honest failure: whatever rung ran out, the goal lands on ONE status (gapped) with the prior status kept as ps_gap_reason (effects are sequential; the copy reads the pre-overwrite value -- probed).

rules.name: ps_gap_file
rules.comment: FILE the gap through the standing pipeline: SelfConcern{kind:'code_write', source:'implicit', status:'noted'} -- the EXACT node shape seeds/code_write_gap.json mints, so the surfacing reader and the human-gated promote spine find it with zero new plumbing. Content-deduped (the note_code_write_gap guard, verbatim pattern). v1.2.0 (P7-A): descent sub-goals (ps_depth >= 1) are EXCLUDED -- a hole's gap is descent-internal working state, not a standalone concern; the OUTER goal files if the whole request gaps. Goals without ps_depth (legacy paths) still file.

rules.name: ps_gap_dedup_mark
rules.comment: The dedup arm: an identical gap is already filed -- mark this goal filed WITHOUT minting (the rule declines to re-file; the agent's own decision, gap_awareness dedup precedent).

rules.name: ps_accept
rules.comment: ACCEPT: a verified goal mints EXACTLY ONE graph-resident Program{name, program} node (the established convention -- program is the hub-IR Term-JSON string) carrying full provenance (construction, attempts). Mint-once via the accepted_program edge count. The adapter's read_off links the ALREADY-REFLECTED IR subgraph root onto the Program (ir_subgraph edge) -- both representations, documented. v1.7.0 (Arc4-S2): gated on structural clearance for TOP-LEVEL goals (ps_depth==0.0) -- ps_structural_reject must read 0.0 (ps_structural_clear already ran). A sub-goal (ps_depth != 0.0, P7-A/P7-B descent holes) is UNCHANGED -- the structural rung is scoped to the measured top-level population (PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC4_STRUCTURAL_NOTES.md) and never touches a descend hole's own fold-up accept. ADDENDUM: the gate is also bypassed when ps_rung_descend==1.0 -- a top-level goal that engaged descent is scoped OUT of the structural rung entirely (compute_structural_facts never runs for it), so ps_structural_reject would otherwise never be set and ps_accept would stall; this third OR-arm keeps such goals byte-unchanged. v1.11.0 (Arc6-D): the third Or-arm now ALSO requires ps_property_reject==0.0 -- a top-level, non-descended goal must clear BOTH the D1-D3 structural detectors AND the theorem-derived PropertyAtom checks (ps_property_reject/ps_property_clear, compute_property_facts) before it may accept. Byte-unchanged for every goal outside that scope (sub-goal / descended), and for any goal ps_property_reject was never set on (compute_property_facts never ran) -- see ps_property_clear's own scope guard.

rules.name: ps_structural_reject_exclusion_gap
rules.comment: Arc4-S6 REJECT INFORMS REPAIR (D1/D2, unreopenable source): D1 memo_lookup_table and/or D2 dead_code_free_vars fired -- per PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC4_S6_NOTES.md Sec.1, NEITHER detector names a single declared parameter to hand to a hole-reopen: D1's fault is the WHOLE CANDIDATE (a memoised lookup table has no correct sub-part to salvage) and D2's fault is a reference to something that isn't a declared input at all (no site to swap it for). The honest response for both is EXCLUSION, not repair -- but exclusion only helps when ps_propose can find a genuinely DIFFERENT next candidate under it. `ps_construction=='retrieved_exemplar'` means it can't (every retrieval accept shares that ONE literal construction name regardless of which exemplar produced it -- excluding it can't distinguish candidates and measured live as the S2 stall, PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC4_S2_NOTES.md Sec.4, task 267). So THIS rung goes straight to the honest terminal: 'gapped' (ps_gap_reason := 'structural_verdict_reject'), route='exclusion' recorded on the Rejection for explainability even though it was never enacted. See ps_structural_reject_exclusion_reopen for the reopenable twin.

rules.name: ps_structural_reject_exclusion_reopen
rules.comment: Arc4-S6 REJECT INFORMS REPAIR (D1/D2, reopenable source): same D1/D2 detection as ps_structural_reject_exclusion_gap, but ps_construction is NOT 'retrieved_exemplar' -- a codebook/lattice/enumerate rung CAN genuinely propose a different next candidate once this one is excluded (the standing CEGIS spine ps_exclude_failed/ps_reproposal/ps_ce_exhausted/ps_enum_retry_mark already proves this safe for every non-retrieval source; it is the SAME lane a real counterexample-driven exclusion already uses). Route the goal DIRECTLY to 'counterexample' (skipping eval_pending/ps_row_fail/ps_counterexample -- there is no failing revealed row to record, the whole point of a structural trap is that it passes every revealed row; the standing rules downstream only ever key on status=='counterexample' + the Excluded/ps_rung_enumerate facts, never on a CounterExample node's existence, so this is a safe, minimal reuse of the existing `exclude` contract per CLAUDE.md's 'extend Rust only if the DSL cannot express it' -- it can). route='exclusion' (no repair localization: D1/D2 have none to hand). Mint-once per candidate: status leaves 'verified' in this same firing, so re-matching cannot duplicate the Rejection.

rules.name: ps_structural_reject_repair_gap
rules.comment: Arc4-S6 REJECT INFORMS REPAIR (D3 only, unreopenable source): D3 unread_declared_param fired ALONE (D1/D2 did not) -- D3 is the detector that DOES name a precise, localizable fault ('ignores declared parameter c', ps_st_varying_unread_params), a strictly better diagnosis than any counterexample (it names the defect instead of exhibiting one failing row). route='repair' is recorded with repair_target_param carrying the ignored parameter(s) even though, on a retrieval-sourced accept, there is nothing for it to reopen against (same S2-stall reason as the D1/D2 twin) -- the honest terminal is still 'gapped'. See ps_structural_reject_repair_reopen for the reopenable twin, which is where this localization actually gets used.

rules.name: ps_structural_reject_repair_reopen
rules.comment: Arc4-S6 REJECT INFORMS REPAIR (D3 only, reopenable source) -- THE residual this phase closes (PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC4_S5.md Sec.7, PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC4_S2_NOTES.md Sec.4): D3 unread_declared_param fired alone, ps_construction is NOT 'retrieved_exemplar', so the codebook/lattice/enumerate rung that produced this candidate can genuinely propose a different one. route='repair', repair_target_param := ps_st_varying_unread_params (the ignored parameter(s), handed to the Rejection instead of thrown away). Routes DIRECTLY to 'counterexample' -- the SAME reused `exclude` contract as the D1/D2 twin (ps_exclude_failed/ps_reproposal/ps_ce_exhausted/ps_enum_retry_mark, unchanged); for an enumerate-sourced candidate (br_10_top_of_three's own shape -- Max(a,b) ignoring c) this is EXACTLY the arc2-Q4 exclude-powered enum-retry lane, which already independently proved it can converge this precise decoy shape to a holdout-passing program. Idempotent: compute_structural_facts recomputes fresh D1/D2/D3 facts for every new verified candidate (its own ps_ir_reflected-count freshness key), so a repaired candidate that is STILL structurally defective is caught again by this same rule family, never silently accepted.

rules.name: ps_structural_clear
rules.comment: Arc4-S2 VERDICT DISCRIMINATION: the adapter (compute_structural_facts) mechanically walked the CURRENT verified candidate's reflected Term subgraph (Term.* nodes / child.* edges) plus the goal's own revealed ExampleRows and recorded D1/D2/D3's raw facts as FIXED-FORMULA goal attrs (the ps_reflect_ok / cmp_ok precedent) -- the adapter never decided anything. THIS rule reads those facts and decides: none of D1 memo_lookup_table / D2 dead_code_free_vars / D3 unread_declared_param fired -> the candidate is structurally clean, clear the gate ps_accept reads. Scoped to top-level goals (ps_depth==0.0) -- a descend hole's own fold-up accept is untouched, byte-identical to pre-v1.7.0 (PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC4_STRUCTURAL_NOTES.md measured these three detectors' recall/precision only on top-level FULL-R3 accepts).

rules.name: ps_property_clear
rules.comment: Arc6-D PROPERTY VERDICT DISCRIMINATION: the adapter (compute_property_facts, domains/prog_property.py) mechanically matched the goal's own prompt text against the held PropertyAtom table (seeds/program_properties.json), SELF-VERIFIED each candidate atom against the goal's OWN revealed rows (a property the revealed data contradicts is refused before it can even be checked -- the refutability gate), and executed the CURRENT verified candidate's reflected IR at each surviving atom's hand-constructed witnesses -- the adapter never decided anything. THIS rule reads those facts and decides: no property atom fired -> the candidate is property-clean, clear the gate ps_accept ALSO reads (beside ps_structural_clear). Scoped to top-level goals (ps_depth==0.0), non-descended -- a descend hole's own fold-up accept is untouched, byte-identical to pre-v1.11.0.

rules.name: ps_property_reject_gap
rules.comment: Arc6-D PROPERTY VERDICT (unreopenable source): a held PropertyAtom (seeds/program_properties.json) fired -- the CURRENT verified candidate's own executed output disagrees, at a hand-constructed witness, with a reference relation the goal's own revealed rows already self-verify (domains/prog_property.py::compute_property_facts / _self_verify_atom). Sits BESIDE ps_structural_reject_exclusion_gap: a property violation, like D1/D2, names no single declared parameter to hand to a hole-reopen (the fault is in what the whole candidate COMPUTES at the witness, not in one ignored input), and on a 'retrieved_exemplar' source ps_propose cannot distinguish a next candidate from this one (the S2-stall reason ps_structural_reject_exclusion_gap already documents) -- so this rung goes straight to the honest terminal 'gapped' (ps_gap_reason := 'property_verdict_reject'), route='exclusion' recorded on the Rejection for explainability even though it was never enacted. See ps_property_reject_reopen for the reopenable twin. v1.12.0 (PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_PROPERTY_REJECT_SURVEY, 2026-08-16): gained ONE extra AND-clause -- (ps_rung_enumerate==1.0 OR the enumerate reserve lane is exhausted) -- so this rule now fires ONLY after the new sibling rule `ps_property_reject_retrieval_enumerate_fallback` has had its one-shot chance to try SynthEnumerate as an independent second candidate source (or was structurally ineligible to). The two rules partition the space exactly (each gains the other's negation), so this remains byte-identical for every goal where the fallback already ran or could not apply -- the terminal 'gapped'/'property_verdict_reject' outcome for the 24/26 population where enumerate's own candidate ALSO violates the property is completely unchanged.

rules.name: ps_property_reject_retrieval_enumerate_fallback
rules.comment: PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_PROPERTY_REJECT_SURVEY (2026-08-16): a held PropertyAtom fired against a retrieved_exemplar candidate -- exactly ps_property_reject_gap's own trigger -- but UNLIKE that terminal rule, enumerate has not yet been tried for this goal (ps_rung_enumerate != 1.0) and the Arc4-S1 isolated enumerate-reserve lane has headroom (retrieval never touches it). Live-verified (PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_PROPERTY_REJECT_SURVEY_RESULTS.md): across the FULL 26-task property_verdict_reject population, SynthEnumerate finds an independent candidate for 26/26; re-checking THAT candidate against the SAME fired PropertyAtom(s) (domains/prog_property.py::check_property, the identical held reference relation + witnesses that rejected the RETRIEVED candidate) separates the 2 tasks where enumerate's candidate is ACTUALLY CORRECT (clears the property) from the 24 where it is ALSO wrong (still violates it) with 100% precision and 100% recall -- zero exceptions. This rule does not accept anything itself: it only ADMITS the goal into the enumerate rung, byte-identically to ps_enumerate_mark's own effects (rung mark, status, reserve bump). The already-shipped, unchanged downstream pipeline (run_enumerate -> eval_and_record -> compute_structural_facts -> compute_property_facts -> ps_property_clear/ps_accept, OR -> ps_property_reject_gap again if the new candidate ALSO violates) is what actually decides accept vs terminal gap, exactly as it already does for every non-retrieval construction path (compute_property_facts's own docstring: 'on every path (codebook, enumerate, retrieval, fold-up)'). Deliberately bypasses the ps_exclude_failed/ps_reproposal CEGIS spine (RETRIEVAL_FALLTHROUGH_RESULTS.md's own S2-stall precedent: excluding 'retrieved_exemplar' by NAME there leaves ps_propose nothing to offer, 'pipeline_stall_nonterminal_status' -- the documented reason ps_property_reject_gap routes straight to gapped instead of reopening). Mutually exclusive with the edited ps_property_reject_gap by construction (see that rule's own updated comment) -- no third, stalled state is reachable. CORRECTION (found live, this same rung): the goal's ps_prop_computed/ps_st_computed flags are UNCONDITIONALLY set 1.0 by compute_property_facts/compute_structural_facts on every run and NEVER reset by any rule -- a previously-latent race in the shared verdict machinery, discovered live by this rung: within ONE run_rules() fixpoint pass, ps_row_pass can flip status straight back to 'verified' for the NEW (enumerate) candidate, and ps_property_reject_gap/ps_property_clear /ps_structural_reject_exclusion_gap/ps_structural_clear/ps_accept would then immediately read the STILL-1.0, STILL-stale ps_prop_computed/ps_st_computed flags (and the fired/witness facts attached to them) left over from the FIRST (retrieved) candidate, one full run_rules() fixpoint BEFORE compute_property_facts/compute_structural_facts (Python verbs, dispatched only after run_rules() reaches fixpoint each round) ever get a chance to recompute for the new n_reflected count. Live-verified: without this reset, task 17 read back gap_reason=property_verdict_reject with the ORIGINAL retrieved candidate's violation still recorded, even though ps_ir held the freshly-enumerated, ACTUALLY-CORRECT candidate. Explicitly resetting both computed-flags to 0.0 here (this rule is the one initiating the second candidate, so it is the correct place to invalidate the first candidate's cached verdict) forces the decision rules to wait one more round for the verbs to refresh, exactly as they already do for a goal's FIRST candidate (where these flags start unset). This race is a general property of the shared freshness-key design, not specific to this rule -- PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_PROPERTY_REJECT_ SURVEY_RESULTS.md documents whether it is exercised anywhere else in the currently-measured population; nothing else is touched here.

rules.name: ps_property_reject_reopen
rules.comment: Arc6-D PROPERTY VERDICT (reopenable source): same PropertyAtom detection as ps_property_reject_gap, but ps_construction is NOT 'retrieved_exemplar' -- a codebook/lattice/enumerate rung CAN genuinely propose a different next candidate once this one is excluded (the SAME standing CEGIS spine ps_structural_reject_exclusion_reopen already reuses: ps_exclude_failed/ps_reproposal/ps_ce_exhausted/ps_enum_retry_mark). Routes DIRECTLY to 'counterexample' -- there is no failing revealed row to record (the whole point of a self-detected trap is that it passes every revealed row); the downstream rules only ever key on status=='counterexample' + the Excluded/ps_rung_enumerate facts, never on a CounterExample node's existence. route='exclusion' (no repair localization: a property violation names no single parameter to hand to a hole-reopen). Mint-once per candidate: status leaves 'verified' in this same firing, so re-matching cannot duplicate the Rejection.

rules.name: ps_descend_mark
rules.comment: P7-A RUNG 2 -- DESCEND (Occam-ordered between the codebook/lattice rungs and whole-goal enumerate): the decode's coverage assignment IS the plan; partial cover is segmentation-by-recognition, not failure. Fires when the codebook rung is spent (NO eligible non-excluded construction remains) but the codebook still COVERS part of the request (trigger match, exclusions ignored -- plan-level exclusion retires a WHOLE-goal plan, not the part as skeleton material), the spec has example rows AND at least one row carries a LIST input (exactly the whole-goal enumerator's inadmissibility boundary: its leaves are scalar, so a list-input spec can NEVER be solved at whole-goal grain -- descent targets precisely the recoverable mass, and every scalar-row path is byte-unchanged), and the depth budget allows (in-frame integer, ps_depth < ps_max_depth). Mark-once via ps_rung_descend. v1.4.0 (Arc2-Q4): the list-input scope guard widens to an Or -- ALSO admits a scalar spec whose SOLE cover is a scalar-accumulation Fold (tmpl_scalar_fold -- a range()-sourced Fold, the factorial/sum-to-n class) or a decided-condition branch (tmpl_branch -- an IfThenElse template, the abs-diff/piecewise class). Byte-unchanged for every pre-Q4 codebook entry (neither attr existed before this version, so the new Or-arm is always false there).

rules.name: ps_plan_fold_step
rules.comment: DESCENT PLAN 1 (finest grain) -- FOLD ACCUMULATOR-STEP HOLE: the decode covered EXACTLY ONE construction and it is a Fold template (tmpl_fold -- a structural fact the adapter stamps mechanically at ensure time, the _normalise_triggers idiom), so the residual is the modification INSIDE the fold: the hole is the per-item step h(acc, x); boundaries come from the decode assignment, never a Python cut. Tried-once per kind via the Not-Exists hole guard; plan_seq is the collision-free counter (the P6.5 lesson applied at sub-goal grain from the start).

rules.name: ps_plan_final_expr
rules.comment: DESCENT PLAN 2 -- FINAL-EXPRESSION HOLE: the covered constructions become live vars v1..vk (their construction templates instantiated over the goal's own inputs -- covered spans instantiate, uncovered spans become the hole) and the hole is the final expression combining them. Runs when the fold-step plan is inapplicable OR was tried and refused/failed (the plan ladder inside the descent rung). Sub-rows are ALWAYS derivable here modulo traps: outer rows over live vars. v1.4.0 (Arc2-Q4): Occam order -- also waits for the branch_arm plan to be inapplicable-or-tried (the SAME 'not applicable OR a hole of that kind already exists' shape as the fold_step clause), so a decided-condition branch tries its dedicated plan first.

rules.name: ps_descend_exhausted
rules.comment: DESCENT EXHAUSTION (honest): every plan on the ladder was tried (the final_expr hole exists -- it is the last plan and always applicable when cover >= 1) or the decode's cover was empty. ps_descend_done opens the whole-goal enumerate gate: a residual that survives every grain reaches the enumerator.

rules.name: ps_hole_derived
rules.comment: The adapter mechanically derived the hole's local example rows (prefix evaluation + record -- arithmetic-free-of-decisions) and recorded the count fact; THIS RULE judges derivability: at least one determinable row -> the hole becomes a sub-goal.

rules.name: ps_hole_underivable
rules.comment: HONEST REFUSAL: no outer row makes this hole's local rows determinable under the documented derivability scopes (named blocker recorded in derive_note). The hole is refused and the descent ladder moves to the next plan.

rules.name: ps_hole_wait
rules.comment: The adapter spawned the sub-spec mechanically (Message + derived ExampleRows -- transcription of THIS ladder's decision, ps_goal mints the sub-Goal exactly like any request). The outer goal now WAITS on the sub-goal's own run of the SAME ladder (recursive solve; fresh integer counters per sub-goal by construction).

rules.name: ps_hole_solved
rules.comment: SUB-ACCEPTANCE: the hole's sub-goal ACCEPTED (ProgEval agreement on ALL derived rows -- the standard verdict pipeline one level down). On to fold-up: execution verdict at every level, so the outer rows still get the final say.

rules.name: ps_hole_failed
rules.comment: SUB-FAILURE: the sub-goal gapped (its own ladder exhausted on the derived rows). The hole fails and the descent ladder moves on -- a bad decomposition dies at the cheapest level.

rules.name: ps_foldup_accept
rules.comment: FOLD-UP VERDICT (accept): the adapter spliced the accepted sub-IR into the skeleton mechanically and re-ran ProgEval over the FULL outer rows into the descent-scoped fu_* lane (NEVER the eval_attempt/verdict_attempt lane -- the P6.5 collision cannot re-arm by construction). Every outer row agrees AND the reflect round-trip holds -> verified; ps_accept mints the Program as usual. Provenance: ps_construction := the covered construction the skeleton instantiated; ps_descend_kind := the hole kind.

rules.name: ps_foldup_reject
rules.comment: FOLD-UP VERDICT (reject): the spliced whole failed an outer row (or the sub-IR was not spliceable). The decomposition is refused -- the outer rows are the execution verdict the derived rows cannot overrule -- and the descent ladder moves to the next plan (then whole-goal enumerate, then gap: honest fall-through).

rules.name: ps_repair_mark
rules.comment: P7-B REPAIR ENTRY (CEGIS at the accept boundary): an ACCEPTED goal holds an example row the adapter mechanically ingested from an external verification failure (ingest_counterexample -- ce_pending, a recorded datum like ps_write_request). THIS RULE decides the accept is REFUTED: the Program keeps its provenance but is marked refuted and the accepted_program edge is retracted (del_edge -- the retire_duplicate_gap precedent), so ps_accept's mint-once guard re-arms for the repaired build. ps_repair_seq increments (integer round counter); the goal moves to trace_pending, where the adapter records boundary facts (prefix evaluations) for the rules to judge. 'ShapeDecode tells you what is going on' applied to diagnosis: the trace against derivable expectations, not a global re-propose.

rules.name: ps_localize_hole
rules.comment: P7-B LOCALIZATION (the fault verdict): the recorded trace is FRESH (ps_trace_seq == ps_repair_seq), every derivable skeleton boundary AGREED with its expectation (ps_trace_skel_agree -- covered constructions re-derived per row, descent's own row-derivation machinery reused), and the divergence pinned the FOLDED hole's grain (ps_trace_diverge_hole -- final_expr: live vars agree, the return diverges; fold_step: a singleton counterexample's one-iteration unroll pins the step and the held body disagrees). The fault = that hole. Repair re-opens ONLY it: the refuted candidate is recorded as an ExcludedSub at hole scope (bounded multi-candidate iteration -- SynthEnumerate is deterministic, so the re-solve's INPUT changes: the derived row set now includes the counterexample's contribution, plus any droppable non-output Lit consts), a NEW Hole of the SAME kind is minted on the collision-free plan_seq counter, and the UNCHANGED descent machinery (derive -> spawn -> sub-solve -> fold-up -> full-row verdict) runs it. The skeleton is NEVER re-proposed. Integer repair budget, own lane.

rules.name: ps_localize_refuse_fresh
rules.comment: P7-B LOCALIZATION HONESTY (never-descended goal): the trace could not pin the fault to a hole (no folded hole -- e.g. a rung-1 codebook accept has no skeleton/hole split; or no derivable expectation -- e.g. a multi-item row against a fold body, the prereg'd non-determinable class; or a skeleton boundary itself diverged). Localization REFUSES and the EXISTING global CEGIS path proceeds unchanged: a fresh integer attempt re-evaluates ALL rows (the counterexample row is among them), ps_row_fail -> ps_counterexample -> exclusion -> re-proposal / exhaustion run exactly as pre-P7B. A goal that never descended keeps every lower rung available.

rules.name: ps_localize_refuse_descended
rules.comment: P7-B LOCALIZATION HONESTY (descended goal): same refusal, plus ps_descend_done := 1 -- the descent rung is spent for this goal (ps_rung_descend == 1 blocks re-entry), so the whole-goal enumerate gate must open or the goal would PARK on pending (the P6.5 zero-parks discipline). Honest fall-through: global re-evaluation -> CEGIS -> enumerate -> gap.

rules.name: ps_repair_exhausted
rules.comment: P7-B BUDGET HONESTY: the trace localizes (a folded hole is pinned) but ps_repair_attempts has reached the integer ps_repair_budget -- no repair round N+1. The goal falls back to the UNTOUCHED global CEGIS path (fresh attempt, all rows re-evaluated, standard counterexample/exclusion/enumerate/gap ladder). ps_descend_done opens the enumerate gate (a folded hole implies the descent rung was consumed).

rules.name: ps_plan_branch_arm
rules.comment: DESCENT PLAN (branch grain, Arc2-Q4) -- BRANCH-ARM HOLES: the decode covered EXACTLY ONE construction and it is an IfThenElse template (tmpl_branch -- the SAME structural-fact idiom as tmpl_fold, stamped mechanically at ensure time): the DECIDED CONDITION is kept from the covered template (the P7-A precedent -- 'double each and total' kept TALLY's fold structure while the body changed; here 'positive difference' keeps max_of_two's a>b while the arms change), and BOTH arms become holes at once. Each arm is solved by a DIRECT SynthEnumerate call over its own row partition (domains/prog_synthesis.py's _derive_branch_arms) rather than a further recursive sub-goal -- the same primitive the whole-goal/hole ladder already uses, applied twice; a genuinely non-trivial partition (BOTH arms non-empty) is required or the plan honestly refuses (never guesses a missing arm). Tried once per goal via the Not-Exists hole guard.

rules.name: ps_branch_arm_ready
rules.comment: BOTH arm holes derived AND both solved (arm_found==1 on each, set by _derive_branch_arms): the branch plan is ready for fold-up (the adapter's fold_up dispatches on the PAIR, reads solved_term_json off each, and builds the recombined IfThenElse).

rules.name: ps_branch_arm_failed
rules.comment: HONEST REFUSAL: the partition was trivial (one side empty) or either arm's own SynthEnumerate call found nothing -- the branch plan is refused (never a guessed arm) and the ladder falls to the next plan (final_expr, then whole-goal enumerate, then gap).

rules.name: ps_enum_retry_mark
rules.comment: P7-B RESIDUAL 2, CLOSED (Arc2-Q4, via the Q1 engine `exclude` contract): a REPAIR counterexample refuted a FLAT rung-3 accept (ps_rung_enumerate==1, no folded hole -- a descended accept is handled by the hole-scope exclude wiring in run_enumerate instead) and the dedicated round budget (ps_enum_round/ps_enum_round_budget -- its OWN counter lane, never ps_attempts/ps_budget) has rounds left: the refuted candidate's return-expression Term-JSON (ps_enum_last_term_json, recorded by run_enumerate) is minted as an ExcludedTerm and the goal returns DIRECTLY to enumerate_pending (bypassing ps_enumerate_mark's permanent mark-once guard on purpose -- ps_rung_enumerate keeps its existing 'engaged at least once' meaning for ps_no_shape's fallback) with a FRESH attempt number (the P6.5 fresh-attempt idiom, so the whole eval/verdict pipeline re-arms cleanly). run_enumerate then passes EVERY accumulated ExcludedTerm as the engine's `exclude` list on the re-enumeration -- genuine within-round candidate iteration. Mutually exclusive with ps_exclude_failed/ps_ce_exhausted by construction (each gains this predicate's negation; pre-Q4 this predicate can never be true, so both stay byte-identical there).

rules.name: ps_row_pass_special
rules.comment: PER-ROW VERDICT (pass), tol/unordered rows: the recorded comparison fact cmp_ok (a fixed formula -- float-within-tolerance or set/duplicate-insensitive equality, per Q2's mbpp_spec row schema) says PASS. Mirrors ps_row_pass exactly, scoped to rows carrying either flag (mutually exclusive with the ORIGINAL rule via its added Not-guard).

rules.name: ps_row_fail_special
rules.comment: PER-ROW VERDICT (fail), tol/unordered rows: trap/non-halt OR the recorded comparison fact cmp_ok says FAIL. Mirrors ps_row_fail exactly, scoped to special rows.

rules.name: ps_goal_top
rules.comment: GOAL MINT (top-level, Arc3-R1): the SAME mint as ps_goal, for a TOP-LEVEL request (ps_depth==0) only -- mints Goal{status:retrieve_pending} instead of pending, so a top-level request enters the retrieval ladder (score -> select top-k -> adapt a/b/c/d, every candidate screened) BEFORE the arc-2 codebook/enumerate/descend stack, which it falls through to (via `pending`, STALE PROSE FIXED Arc3-R2.5 -- the codebook-side screen never used a distinct `screen_pending` status; see ps_lattice_failed's comment) -- unchanged on retrieval exhaustion, modulo Arc3-R2.5's OWN scoped codebook screen now engaging on `pending` for SCREENABLE goals. Also mints `ps_screen_pool0` (the initial trigger-matching codebook pool count, frozen here so the screen's own slack comparison never drifts as candidates are excluded). Also mints the pr_screen_* universal-screen counter lane (own integers, separate from ps_attempts/ps_repair_*/ps_enum_round* by the same P6.5 collision discipline) and pr_topk (the retrieval top-k bound).

rules.name: pr_select_candidate
rules.comment: ARC3-R1 RANKED RETRIEVAL -- SELECTION IS A RULE. `score_exemplars` (adapter, mechanical arithmetic) boarded one ScoreLink{score, task_id, picked:0.0} proxy per held Exemplar, linked g-pr_score->sl-pr_score_exemplar->exemplar (a proxy node so the winning exemplar can be bound as a real match-var for add_edge -- the engine's add_edge effect requires a bound var, never a Term-computed target). This rule picks the CURRENT best unpicked ScoreLink (no other unpicked sl2 has a strictly higher score, or an equal score with a lower task_id -- a strict total order, so exactly one sl wins per round) and mints ONE g-pr_candidate->exemplar edge, bounded by pr_topk (5). Successive fixpoint rounds pick the next-best remaining, giving a deterministic top-k in rank order (read back by `_candidate_pool`'s edge-insertion-order reliance).

rules.name: pr_ladder_ready
rules.comment: Selection is done -- either pr_topk candidates are picked, or every held Exemplar has been considered (fewer than pr_topk exist, or none scored at all) -- hand off to run_retrieval_ladder.

rules.name: pr_ladder_accept
rules.comment: The retrieval ladder (adapter, run_retrieval_ladder) found a screen-passing candidate at SOME rung (a-d) -- hand its IR to the UNCHANGED eval_pending -> evaluated -> ps_row_pass/fail -> ps_verified -> ps_accept chain (a retrieval accept is verified by the EXACT SAME execution machinery a codebook/enumerate accept is). Consumes exactly ONE ps_attempts unit -- screening itself never touched ps_attempts, so attempts-per-accept does not rise (HR2).

rules.name: pr_ladder_fallthrough
rules.comment: The retrieval ladder exhausted its top-k candidates at every rung (a-d) without a screen-passing adapt -- fall through to the arc-2 stack UNCHANGED, via screen_pending (the universal screen now guards the codebook rung's first pick too). REVISED: hands off directly to pending (not screen_pending) -- the codebook-side universal screen (pr_screen_*) was attempted and REVERTED: it produced false negatives on legitimate PARTIAL-COVER constructions (a construction that does not fit ALL revealed rows alone but is the correct descent starting point once a hole is filled in) since the screen only checks whole-row pass/fail with no knowledge of the descent mechanism's own independent ShapeDecode-based partial-cover logic -- excluding such a construction stranded goals with no eligible codebook pick while descent, which does not consult ps_excluded at all, still (correctly) used it via a different path, leaving ps_attempts/ps_rung_codebook never set. Reverted rather than risk this class of regression across the existing descent/repair surface; see PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC3_R12_NOTES.md.

rules.name: ps_screen_mark
rules.comment: Arc3-R2.5 -- THE SCOPED CODEBOOK-SIDE UNIVERSAL SCREEN (the corrected redo of the Attempt-1 screen REVERTED in PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC3_R12_NOTES.md, now ALSO scoped against a second, measured false-positive -- see ps_propose's own comment). Fires only when SCREENABLE(g): NOT DESCEND_APPLICABLE (so every partial-cover-eligible goal is untouched BY CONSTRUCTION, not luck) AND at least one revealed example row exists (nothing to screen against otherwise) AND the INITIAL trigger-matching codebook pool (`ps_screen_pool0`, FROZEN at mint, never recomputed) is NOT smaller than the goal's full attempt budget -- i.e. the classic propose/exclude/reproposal mechanism could NOT try every eligible candidate for real without exhausting the budget before descend/enumerate ever gets a turn. Because the pool figure is frozen (see NO_SLACK's own docstring in the builder script this rule was generated from) the SCREENABLE verdict is effectively a ONE-TIME, PER-GOAL decision: a goal that already had enough slack to succeed unscreened (e.g. 2 trigger-matching decoys against a budget of 3, `br_19_pick_or_boost`'s own shape) is NEVER screened at all, on ANY round; a goal without slack has EVERY eligible candidate screened for free until one passes or none remain -- attempts-per-accept is therefore never made worse than the classic mechanism, only ever equal (a goal with slack) or strictly better (a goal without it), HR2's own non-increasing bar. Marks the goal's current specificity-Argmax winner (the SAME formula ps_propose's own effect uses, restricted to the not-yet-screened pool) as `ps_screen_candidate` and hands off to the `screen_running` adapter verb (domains/prog_synthesis.py:screen_construction), a dry-run mirror of splice_binding's own template->IR logic that spends NO ps_attempts.

rules.name: ps_screen_reject
rules.comment: Arc3-R2.5: the screened candidate FAILED at least one revealed row (dry run, no ps_attempts spent) -- excluded exactly like a real failed attempt (ps_lattice_failed/ps_exclude_failed's own Excluded-node pattern), tagged `screened_failed:1.0` so the taxonomy can count a screen kill separately from a real counterexample exclusion, then re-armed to `pending` so ps_screen_mark/ps_propose re-decide against the shrunk pool -- THIS is the decoy-tax kill: a wrong complete candidate never reaches ps_propose, so it never costs a real attempt, exactly where (per ps_screen_mark's own SCREENABLE gate) it would otherwise have guaranteed exhaustion before descend/enumerate ever ran. Gated by `ps_screen_name == ps_screen_candidate` (see `_fresh_verdict`'s own docstring in the builder script) so a stale verdict from an earlier candidate this SAME fixpoint round can never be mistaken for this one's.

rules.name: ps_screen_admit
rules.comment: Arc3-R2.5: the screened candidate PASSED every revealed row (dry run, no ps_attempts spent) -- minted as a ScreenPass marker (`g -ps_screen_passed-> sp{name}`, the ps_excluded proxy-node idiom) and re-armed to `pending`, where ps_propose's now-satisfied screen-bypass Or picks the SAME winner up (the specificity Argmax is unchanged and deterministic, so it is guaranteed to re-select this exact construction) and spends EXACTLY one real attempt on it -- a candidate already known to fit every revealed row, so that attempt is a real accept, not a decoy burn. Gated by `ps_screen_name == ps_screen_candidate` (see `_fresh_verdict`'s own docstring in the builder script), the SAME freshness guard `ps_screen_reject` carries.

rules.name: ps_isolate_fallthrough
rules.comment: Arc4-S1 BUDGET ISOLATION: the propose lane (codebook + retrieval; ps_propose_attempts/ps_propose_budget) is spent for this goal -- the SAME state ps_ce_exhausted's own 'BUDGET HONESTY at the propose gate' would otherwise terminally exhaust -- but this is a first-pass goal (ps_repair_entered never set; the P7-B repair loop's own 'global CEGIS path' fallback reuses ps_ce_exhausted/ps_reproposal UNCHANGED and is never redirected here) AND a next rung is still reachable: EITHER descent is still applicable (a list-input or scalar-fold/branch cover exists, depth budget allows, descent never entered -- class (a), 7 ids: PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC4_S0A_NOTES.md) OR the RESERVED, untouchable enumerate lane still has room (class (b), 10 ids, the screen's own documented 'goal with initial slack is never screened' residual). Re-arms to 'pending' so ps_descend_mark / ps_enumerate_mark -- whose OWN entry guards no longer depend on the shared ps_attempts/ps_budget lane -- get their turn. This is ISOLATION, not screening: no candidate's correctness is judged here (unlike the Arc3-R12 Attempt-1 screen, which evaluated partial-cover candidates as complete programs and produced false negatives) -- only which BUDGET COUNTER gates entry into the next rung changes. Mutually exclusive with ps_ce_exhausted by construction: both share the identical base state (kind, status==counterexample, exclusion just applied, Gte(ps_attempts,ps_budget), the SAME enum-retry carve-out copied verbatim) and then test a single shared predicate and its exact negation.

rules.name: ps_exact_mark
rules.comment: RUNG 2.5 -- EXACT-FIRST (PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC5_EXACT_FIRST.md), Occam-ordered BETWEEN descent and enumerate: shape -> IR, ahead of blind syntax search. Fires only when (a) NO eligible codebook construction remains OR propose is exhausted (the SAME first Or-arm ps_enumerate_mark itself embeds -- copied verbatim so this rung engages at EXACTLY the point enumerate would have, never earlier), (b) example rows exist, (c) the Message's own `ps_exact_eligible` fact (ingest_spec: numeric, FLOAT-typed expected, arity 1..3 -- domains/prog_synthesis.py's `_examples_numeric_eligible`) is true, (d) descend is done or not applicable (the SAME Or-arm ps_enumerate_mark embeds, copied verbatim -- a partial-cover list-input spec still gets first crack at descent), and (e) this rung has never run for this goal (`ps_rung_exact`, a plain once-only flag -- no separate reserved-budget lane; unlike enumerate this rung never needs one, since a fit costs no propose-lane attempt either way). The adapter (`run_exact_family`) evaluates `domains.prog_exact`'s bounded search against the held ExactFamily seed data and records ONE outcome fact (`ps_exact_outcome`); `ps_exact_solved`/`ps_exact_failed` decide everything downstream.

rules.name: ps_exact_solved
rules.comment: The exact-first rung's adapter (`run_exact_family`) fit a held ExactFamily to every revealed row and spliced the rendered IR for THIS attempt (`ps_ir_built == ps_attempts`, the `ps_enumerated` precedent verbatim): the recovered candidate goes through the SAME execution verdict as every other build -- ps_verify -> structural detectors -> ps_accept, unchanged.

rules.name: ps_exact_failed
rules.comment: No held ExactFamily fit every revealed row within its (declared or implied) tolerance: honest failure, back to `pending` -- `ps_rung_exact` is already stamped so this rule (and `ps_exact_mark`) can never re-fire for this goal, and the very next rung the Occam ladder tries is enumerate (`ps_enumerate_mark`'s own guard is otherwise unaffected by this rung ever having run). NOT a terminal status -- the SAME 'try the next rung' shape `ps_screen_reject` and `ps_lattice_failed` already use.

rules.name: ps_move_mark
rules.comment: RUNG 2.6 -- STRUCTURAL MOVES (PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC5_MOVES.md): orbit augmentation (MOVE A, PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC5_ORBIT_RESULT.md) and intermediate decomposition (MOVE B, task 59 in PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC5_THREE_MOVES.md), selected by WEIGHTED COLLAPSE rather than a fixed ladder -- both feed the SAME MoveCandidate pool and the SAME ps_move_select Argmax. Fires under EXACTLY the entry conditions ps_exact_mark itself embeds (copied verbatim: no eligible codebook construction remains or propose is exhausted; example rows exist; descend is done or inapplicable), PLUS (a) the exact rung is RESOLVED for this goal -- ps_rung_exact==1 (it ran, whatever the outcome) OR the goal was never exact-eligible at all (ps_exact_eligible!=1, so ps_exact_mark's own guard could never have fired) -- structural mutual exclusion with RUNG 2.5, never a reliance on engine tie-break order between two independently-guarded rules; (b) the Message's own ps_moves_eligible fact (domains/prog_moves.py moves_eligible -- numeric/integer type-level pre-filter for either move family); (c) this rung has never run for this goal (ps_rung_moves, mint-once, no separate reserved-budget lane -- a scored-but-unselected candidate costs no propose-lane attempt, same as the exact rung). Stamps the WEIGHT COEFFICIENTS onto the goal itself (ps_move_w_gap/ps_move_w_arity/ps_move_w_mdl) -- graph data the ps_move_select Argmax reads, tunable per-goal without touching any rule or Python code.  v1.12.0 (goal residuals): also stamps ps_move_w_residual -- the coefficient on the HELD-REFUTATION term ps_move_select subtracts.  Same shape as the other three: graph data on the goal, tunable without touching a rule or a line of Python.

rules.name: ps_move_select
rules.comment: WEIGHTED COLLAPSE: Argmax over every candidate MoveCandidate attached to this goal (has_move_candidate) that is BOTH un-refuted AND demonstrates a strictly positive gap (an EARNS-ITS-KEEP gate -- PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC5_MOVES.md: a move that changes nothing about the reachable search must not preempt blind search; this is the fix for the collateral interception measured against several trivially-factorable/already-symmetric fixtures elsewhere in the regression suite -- see the results doc), by weight = ps_move_w_gap*gap + ps_move_w_arity*arity_gap - ps_move_w_mdl*mdl_bits -- coefficients read from the GOAL's own attrs (graph data ps_move_mark stamped, tunable without code or rule changes). Refutation and the gap>0 gate are BOTH pool-membership filters, never weight terms (PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC5_ORBIT_RESULT.md sec 3: refutation is 'never a low score'). Both MOVE A (orbit_augment) and MOVE B (intermediate_factor) candidates sit in the SAME pool -- there is no rung ordering between them, only the weight. Copies the winner's identifying facts onto the goal (ps_move_sel_kind/ps_move_sel_key/ps_move_sel_gap/ps_move_sel_arity_gap/ps_move_sel_mdl) so the selection is auditable, then hands off to apply_selected_move (status=move_apply_pending).  v1.12.0 (GOAL RESIDUALS -- measured ceilings, graph-resident): the weight gains one more term, `- ps_move_w_residual * PENALTY(mc)`, where PENALTY is the weight of the STRONGEST non-stale GoalResidual whose goal signature matches this candidate's (0.0 when none does, so the term is identically absent for every unsignatured candidate -- which is every candidate prog_moves.py mints today).  A refutation the agent already holds is a WEIGHT, not a veto: it is subtracted INSIDE the Argmax and appears NOWHERE in the pool filters, so a candidate with a large enough gap still wins over a held residual.  Pursuing an unreachable goal is legitimate -- that is how residuals get made; being confidently wrong where the residual is already held is not.  The penalty is computed INLINE rather than read from an attr, so the selection can never depend on whether gr_move_penalty's audit stamp has been written yet in the fixpoint; gr_move_sel_audit (seeds/goal_residuals.json) copies the winner's charge onto the goal afterwards.

rules.name: ps_move_none
rules.comment: No candidate MoveCandidate survives BOTH the refutation veto AND the gap>0 earns-its-keep gate -- honest fall-through to 'pending' so the very next rung (enumerate) tries the ORIGINAL, unaugmented rows. ps_rung_moves is already stamped (mint-once), so this rung can never re-engage for this goal. NOT a terminal status -- the SAME 'try the next rung' shape ps_exact_failed/ps_screen_reject already use.

rules.name: ps_move_fresh_attempt
rules.comment: THE P6.5 STALL FIX, applied to RUNG 2.6 (the ps_enumerate_fresh_attempt precedent, verbatim structure): when apply_selected_move's intermediate_factor branch follows a CONSUMED codebook attempt (a codebook candidate proposed, evaluated and rejected BEFORE the moves rung ever got a turn), the example rows already carry eval_attempt == ps_attempts, so eval_and_record's own ps_eval_done == ps_attempts guard would silently treat the move's freshly-composed IR as 'already evaluated this attempt' and never actually run it — the goal parks on the non-terminal 'evaluated' status with STALE per-row facts from the earlier, unrelated codebook candidate (verified live: MBPP task 162 reproduced this exact stall before this rule existed). On move_apply_pending, iff some example row's eval_attempt equals the goal's CURRENT ps_attempts (the exact collision that defines the defect -- nothing else), ps_attempts += 1 (in-frame integer step) BEFORE apply_selected_move ever reads it. Self-extinguishing (the bump falsifies its own Exists guard) and naturally single-shot (the adapter verb dispatched on this SAME status always transitions status away in the same round, so the goal never revisits move_apply_pending). Orbit-augmentation's own hand-off (status='pending', letting the UNCHANGED enumerate rung run) is unaffected either way -- ps_enumerate_fresh_attempt already covers that rung's own collision independently.
